- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot after spikes.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays response to sentiment shifts, especially after strong negative sentiment.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to overprediction in subsequent periods.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment is diverging — model overfits short-term momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to underpredict upward moves — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for such cases.
